about: Proposed text_blocks.read_aloud overrides for screen and figure blocks: a short spoken description used by narration instead of the block's HTML. Drafted with model help from text_blocks.data.fields and the surrounding prose. Each is pinned to the block's sha256; if the block changes, the override no longer applies. status 'unreviewed' means no person has signed off yet.

overrides.read_aloud: The circle shows: Veridian Parliament. Proof of invitation verified.

The diagram centers on airborne disease resistance, with a dashed line leading up to the rest of the portfolio. It splits into five branches: air quality at twenty-four percent, early detection at twenty-two, treatment at twenty-one, prophylactics at twenty, and individual non-pharmaceutical prevention at eight. Each branch splits again: air quality mostly into ventilation and filtration, with fourteen percent to ultraviolet light; early detection into wastewater scanning, airborne environment scanning, individual testing and social media open-source analysis; treatment mostly into antivirals; prophylactics mostly into vaccines; and prevention mostly into masks, with smaller shares for nose sprays and saline nasal rinsing. From every one of those, more lines run off past the edge of the screen.

Zoomed in on ultraviolet light, which gets fourteen percent of the air quality portfolio. Forty-five percent of that goes to improving the efficiency of two hundred twenty-two nanometer lamps, thirty percent to safety testing of those lamps, and fifteen percent to upper-room deployment. Below those sit named projects and labs: Dalias and colleagues, Poppe and Mawart, and Vidrik under krypton chloride lamps; Bonne under alternative lamp designs; Kudlin and Melana, studying effects on household chemicals; and Pov and Imerry, and the V N U Aeronautics Lab, under deployment. The V N U Materials Science Lab is funded from two branches at once: alternative lamp designs, and safety testing.

The ballot is titled Rubric: openness in hardware, and lists three motions, each with Yes and No buttons. The first adds a line to tiers one and two: Products in military, surveillance and counter-surveillance applications are not eligible for this tier. The second raises the tax brackets from zero, six, twelve, eighteen and twenty-four, to zero, ten, twenty, twenty-six and thirty-two. The third changes a line in tiers four and five from use of hardware means to prevent third-party repair, to use of hardware or software means to prevent third-party repair.
